We evaluate with metrics as diverse as possible. First, we consider reference-based metrics: ROUGE-2, which measures bigram overlap, BERTScore, which measures semantic similarity with BERT embeddings, and A3CU, which extracts facts in the form of Atomic Content Units (ACUs), and checks the presence of ACUs between prediction and reference. As reference-free metrics, we include SummaC, a leading factual consistency evaluation metric relying on entailment scores between pairs of source and summary sentences. We also leverage GPT-3.5 again (still gpt-3.5-turbo-0125), this time as a summarization evaluator...

We also leverage GPT-3.5 again (still gpt-3.5-turbo-0125), this time as a summarization evaluator, which is proven to be a strong natural language generation evaluator. We prompt the model with the source and generated summary (which fits in GPT-3.5's 16k context window) and ask to output a score on a likert scale from 1 to 5.
